text: Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and the writer no sooner recalls the earlier promise than he turns it into a test. Much of the weight of the scene falls upon a single word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel, and which means something different at every repetition. It costs him more each time. The word that declares his presence is the word by which he gives up Isaac.
